record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.original_question: Was the electroweak phase transition in the early Universe first order, or more specifically strongly first order with v(Tc)/Tc ≳ 1 at the critical temperature Tc, so that electroweak baryogenesis was possible? If it was first order, what new degrees of freedom near the electroweak scale, coupled non-negligibly to the Higgs field, produced the barrier between the electroweak-symmetric and electroweak-breaking minima?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Standard Model of particle physics extended, possibly, by additional degrees of freedom near the electroweak scale (around 100 GeV–1 TeV) that couple non-negligibly to the Higgs doublet Φ. In the early Universe at temperatures of order 100 GeV, the thermal effective potential V_eff(Φ, T) governs the transition between the electroweak-symmetric phase ⟨Φ⟩ = 0 and the electroweak-breaking phase ⟨Φ⟩ = v/√2 ≠ 0. Within the pure Standard Model (with the measured Higgs boson mass ≈ 125 GeV), the electroweak transition is known to be a smooth crossover.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether the actual electroweak phase transition in the early Universe was first order, in the sense that V_eff(Φ, T_c) develops two degenerate minima separated by a barrier at some critical temperature T_c.

(b) Determine whether the transition was strongly first order in the sense
   v(T_c) / T_c ≳ 1,
where v(T_c) is the Higgs VEV in the broken minimum at T_c. (This is the standard sphaleron-decoupling condition required for successful electroweak baryogenesis, i.e., for the baryon asymmetry generated during bubble nucleation to be preserved against electroweak sphaleron washout in the broken phase.)

(c) If the transition was first order, identify the new degrees of freedom near the electroweak scale, coupled non-negligibly to the Higgs field, that are responsible for producing the barrier between the electroweak-symmetric minimum and the electroweak-breaking minimum of V_eff(Φ, T_c). Specify the mechanism (e.g., tree-level barrier from additional scalars, thermally-induced cubic terms from new bosonic states, non-perturbative dynamics from a strongly-coupled sector, or a modified Higgs potential from higher-dimensional operators) by which the barrier is generated.
artifact.status_search_result: The nature of the electroweak phase transition remains an open question in particle physics. Within the pure Standard Model with a 125 GeV Higgs, lattice studies (Kajantie et al., and subsequent work) established that the transition is a crossover. Whether new physics renders it (strongly) first order, and which new degrees of freedom would be responsible, is actively investigated and is a primary scientific target of proposed future colliders (HL-LHC, ILC, FCC-ee/hh, CEPC, muon collider) and gravitational-wave observatories (LISA). No definitive experimental determination exists as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Electroweak phase transition - review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews status of the electroweak phase transition; in the SM it is a crossover, but BSM extensions can render it strongly first order; experimental tests via colliders and gravitational waves are discussed as ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether the EWPT is (strongly) first order, and the identification of responsible new physics, remains open and is the target of future experiments.

status_evidence.title: Snowmass report on EWPT and baryogenesis
status_evidence.snippet: The character of the electroweak phase transition is among the key open questions; a strongly first-order transition requires BSM physics coupled to the Higgs.
